previous_disclosures.summary: QCT is a leading developer and supplier of integrated circuits and system software for mobile devices, automotive systems, and IoT. Its technology roadmap results from extensive collaboration with industry partners and research into emerging standards, leveraging foundational mobile technologies to extend into automotive and IoT applications.

The Snapdragon family includes mobile, compute, sound, and automotive platforms comprising application processors, cellular modems, and wireless connectivity capabilities. Key components include Qualcomm Oryon and Kryo CPUs, Hexagon NPUs for AI processing, and Adreno GPUs.

QCT provides wireless connectivity products for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services across mobile devices, automotive, and IoT applications, including standalone Wi-Fi and Bluetooth products. Networking products include Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and PON chips that enable home and business networks.

current_disclosures.summary: QCT develops a technology roadmap for mobile, automotive, and IoT devices through collaboration with industry partners. Its product families include Snapdragon and Dragonwing, which feature application processors (Oryon, Kryo CPUs), Hexagon NPUs, and Adreno GPUs. In addition to core SoCs, QCT supplies supporting components such as RF transceivers, power management ICs, and integrated Snapdragon 5G modem-RF products that use AI. QCT also provides wireless connectivity products for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services, as well as networking products like Wi-Fi and Ethernet chips.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions for mobile devices, including integrated combination chips and location platform services.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO disclose wireless connectivity products for mobile devices, specifically highlighting Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions. QCOM describes its products as integrated circuits for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services supporting mobile devices and IoT, while AVGO provides discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions designed for smartphones and wearables. A key similarity is the emphasis on integration; QCOM mentions standalone Wi-Fi and Bluetooth products, whereas AVGO highlights 'combination chips that offer integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth functionality' for performance advantages. Additionally, AVGO explicitly includes GPS/GNSS in its connectivity suite, which aligns with QCOM's mention of 'location data and services'.

sentences.text: Our wireless connectivity products also consist of integrated circuits and system software for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and frequency modulation, as well as technologies that support location data and services.

Our wireless connectivity products provide additional connectivity for mobile devices, tablets, PCs, XR headsets, voice and music devices, wearable devices, along with other IoT devices and applications, automotive connectivity, digital cockpit and ADAS/AD, utility meters and logistic trackers and industrial sensors.
QCT also offers standalone Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, applications processor and Ethernet products utilized within these devices and systems.

• Connectivity Solutions: Our connectivity solutions include discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions, and global positioning system/global navigation satellite system ("GPS/GNSS") receivers, designed for use in mobile devices including smartphones, tablets and wearable products.
These solutions include combination chips that offer integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth functionality, which provides significant performance advantages over discrete solutions.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides SoC solutions for broadband access applications, including DSL, cable, and PON technologies for consumer and central office deployments.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose networking and broadband access products, specifically mentioning Passive Optical Network (PON) technology. QCOM states that its networking products include 'Wi-Fi, Ethernet and passive optical network (PON) chips' to help enable home and business networks. Similarly, AVGO offers 'complete SoC platform solutions for... passive optical networking ("PON")... for both consumer premise equipment ("CPE") and central office ("CO") deployments.' Both firms target the broadband infrastructure market, with QCOM focusing on the chips and equipment enabling these networks and AVGO providing SoC platforms for DSL, cable, and PON deployments in both residential and central office settings.

sentences.text: Our networking products include Wi-Fi, Ethernet and passive optical network (PON) chips, network processors, wireless access points and routers, broadband gateway equipment and software.
These products help enable home and business networks to support the growing number of connected devices, digital media and data services.

• Broadband Access: We offer complete SoC platform solutions for digital subscriber line ("DSL"), cable, passive optical networking ("PON") and wireless local area network for both consumer premise equipment ("CPE") and central office ("CO") deployments. Our CPE devices are used in broadband modems, residential gateways and Wi-Fi access points and routers. Our CO devices, including DSL Access Multiplexer ("DSLAM"), cable modem termination systems and PON optical line termination medium access controllers, are empowering modern operator broadband infrastructure. Our products enable global service providers to continue deploying next generation broadband access technologies across multiple standards, including G.fast, Data Over Cable Service Interface Specifications ("DOCSIS"), PON and Wi-Fi to provide more bandwidth and faster speeds to consumers.
